dossier.public_summary: The dip does not come from the target star: TESS difference images show it 25 arcseconds away at high significance, well outside the target location. A nearby faint star can mimic the 0.6% dip with a small eclipse, so the signal is best explained as a blended binary, not a planet.

reasons.why: Difference imaging in 5 sectors used places the dip 24.7 arcsec from the target at 14 sigma (err_arcsec 1.756). Inconclusive suspects at 32.7, 41.3, 44.2 arcsec are 5.6 to 13 sigma from centroid, while closest plausible neighbour remains 2.8 arcsec away (eclipse_needed 0.0171) needing 14.7 sigma offset. This is strong evidence the transit is not on the target, requiring a blended eclipsing binary.
Two stars within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can produce the observed depth with eclipses <25%, consistent with a blend at the measured off-target position.
Machine-learned planet rank is much below 0.5 (16th percentile), typical of false positives, reinforcing the centroid blend.
